payload.stem: A researcher wants to estimate the proportion of households with a vegetable garden among the 480 households in a village and has a complete list of the households. The sample size will be $50$. Which of the following plans is most likely to give an estimate that is not biased?

options.text: Post the survey on the village's website and use the answers of the households that choose to respond.
options.why: Volunteers or respondents who choose to reply can differ from the whole population, so the estimate can be biased.

options.text: Survey the first $50$ households that the researcher meets while walking along the main street.
options.why: Selecting the individuals who are easiest to reach leaves out the others and tends to give a biased estimate.

options.text: Number the households on the list from $1$ to $480$, use a random number generator to choose $50$ different numbers, and survey those households.
options.why: Every individual on the complete list has the same chance of being chosen, so the sample tends to represent the whole population.

options.text: Ask the village council to choose $50$ households that it considers typical of the village.
options.why: Selecting individuals that someone considers typical introduces the chooser's judgment and does not give every individual a chance.

options.text: Estimator B, because its sampling distribution has the largest spread and so covers the most possible values.
options.why: Treats a larger spread as an advantage; more variability means estimates that are farther from the parameter more often.

options.text: Estimator A, because it has the smallest spread of all the estimators.
options.why: Considers variability alone; the center of this sampling distribution is not at the true value, so the estimator is biased.

options.text: Estimator D, because the center of its sampling distribution is at the true value and its spread is the smallest among the estimators that are centered there.
options.why: An estimator that is unbiased has a sampling distribution centered at the parameter, and among unbiased estimators the one with the least variability is best.
